newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS AND ZOELLER FINALLY PUT MASTERS REMARKS TO REST.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS AND ZOELLER FINALLY PUT MASTERS REMARKS TO REST.

text.p: Tiger Woods and Fuzzy Zoeller held their long-awaited, face-to-face meeting at Colonial Country Club on Tuesday and both golfers said they hoped they could at last put the Masters incident behind them.
Zoeller drew a firestorm of criticism for his remarks at the conclusion of last month's Masters about what record-setting winner Woods might decide to have served at next year's Champions Dinner.

Zoeller had already publicly apologised for his clumsy stab at humour, but Tuesday's 20-minute lunch in the players dining room was their first face-to-face meeting, one that Woods had said he was looking forward to.

"We had a nice lunch and a nice conversation. I let him know how I feel and heard what he was thinking and now it's behind us," Woods said. "Now I understand the entire situation and hope we can both have a good week this week."
Zoeller who had described his life as "total hell," since the incident, did not appear at Tuesday's news conference, but said he was glad to have the meeting behind him.
"Everything went good and positive. We're looking straight ahead and moving on from here," he said. "I just hope something positive comes from this."
Zoeller said he had briefly considered retiring, but decided to come to Fort Worth and face Woods before this week's $1.6 million Colonial PGA tournament.

Colonial officials had suggested a possible practice round between the two men, but Woods declined, going off late Tuesday afternoon for his first look at the course, which has hosted a PGA tournament since 1946.
Woods's tournament tee time Thursday is nearly three hours later than Zoeller's.
"It's not the worst thing that's ever happened to me and I'm sure it's not going to be the last," Woods said about the Zoeller affair.
In his first appearance since his virtuoso victory a month ago at the Masters, Woods won the Byron Nelson Classic by two shots over Lee Rinker last Sunday.
He will be going for his third straight win this week at the Colonial and his seventh pro victory worldwide, and sixth on the PGA Tour, since leaving the amateur ranks nine months ago.

"My goal is always to get better and that's what I hope to do this week," said Woods, who had his personal swing teacher, Butch Harmon, travel to Fort Worth from Houston to work on his swing before the tournament begins.

"In a weird way, winning last week meant more to me than Augusta (Masters). When you're not hitting it well and you get something out of it that means something. When you're on all cylinders, it's easy to win," said Woods.
A win this week would make Woods the first PGA player since South African Gary Player in 1978 to win three straight tournaments.
"I always expect to win and that's what I have in mind this week," Woods said.
During his four-week vacation following his Masters triumph, Woods played golf with basketball superstar Michael Jordan and visited a movie set with film star Kevin Costner.
After last Sunday's Byron Nelson win, Woods said he got to meet another friend, the Dutchess of York.

"Sarah (Ferguson) and I are very good friends. She has helped me through a lot of things and we've talked a lot on the telephone. I was glad to finally get a chance to meet her in person," said Woods.
After his two-shot victory, Ferguson greeted Woods with a hug and kiss as he was walked off the last green.
Ferguson, in the United States filming a number of television commercials, had diverted her travel plans to stop in Irving, Texas, and watch Woods's final round.
She spent the night in a local hotel and had dinner with Woods' mother Kultida on Saturday night.
"This was my first golf tournament, but I really enjoyed it," Ferguson said. "Mrs. Woods is being a great host and explained everything to me."

A legion of more casual friends will be on hand this week as tournament officials announced a sellout for the first time in the 51-year history of the Colonial event. Ticket sales were cut off after 40,000 badges were sold.
Last week at the Byron Nelson, nearly 100,000 fans watched Woods claim victory.
